newsitem.title: LEBANON: GAMES-SAUDI ATHLETE STRIPPED OF MEDALS FOR DOPING.
newsitem.headline: GAMES-SAUDI ATHLETE STRIPPED OF MEDALS FOR DOPING.

text.p: A Saudi Arabian athlete was stripped of his gold and silver medals in the Pan Arab Games in Beirut on Sunday after being disqualified for doping.
The Arab Sports Federation said in a statement that discus gold medal winner Khaled al-Khalidi tested positive for an unspecified drug in a Paris laboratory.
"The Federation's secretary-general Osman Saad said out of 75 urine samples of track and field winners, only Khalidi's tested positive..," said the statement.
He was the first Arab athlete to lose his prizes on doping grounds since the games opened in Beirut on July 12.

It was the first time that an Arab athlete was stripped of his trophies since the games were launched in 1953 in Alexandria, Egypt, according to a physician in a committee charged with monitoring doping in the games.
Khalidi won the discus gold with a throw of 54.90 metres on Monday. His disqualification will lift Egyptian runner up Sameh Sayyed to first place and Qatari Rashed Doussari to second.
Khalidi also won the silver medal in the shot-put with a throw of 17.64 metres on Tuesday.
He was not available for comment and officials from the Saudi team refused to discuss the incident.

Before the games began in Beirut, the Anti-Doping Committee of The Arab Sports Federation distributed pamphlets to the 2,200 athletes from nineteen countries competing in 20 sports warning them against the use of drugs.
Egypt has won 43 gold medals, Algeria 23, Morocco 12, Qatar 8 and Tunisia 7.
